To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the proposed two-layer linear MPC architecture, equipped with a decuoupling strategy, is a suitable approach to improve the control performance of billets heating process, in terms of quality, safety, energy saving and environment impact.
the use of MPC with a decoupled selection of the manipulated variable can lead to a significant improvement of the control performance in terms of both dynamic and steady state response.

a multivariable model based approach, exploiting the cooperation of a dynamic and a steady-state layer, is able to provide an effective Advanced Process Control module for the regulation of billets heating.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and implementation of a Model Predictive Control strategy for a real industrial process, with particular attention to the input selection issue.
the development of advanced control solutions, based both on the multivariable and on the model-based control approaches, to face the challenging problems of the steel industry.
the development of an advanced process control system, based on Model Predictive Control, for the heating phase of a billet processing in a steel plant.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed approach, based on the decoupling strategy, allows the achievement of an optimal control performance for each controlled output, with a reduced number of manipulated inputs, leading to a significant improvement of the overall process performances.
the proposed architecture has been successfully implemented on the real plant, and has provided a significant improvement of the process performances.
the proposed architecture is a valid and promising alternative to the traditional PID approach for the control of industrial processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed architecture is a promising approach for the development of multivariable Advanced Process Control modules, able to improve the performances of the plant and to reduce energy consumptions.
we have developed a novel two-layer linear Model Based Predictive Control architecture, equipped with a decuoplpling strategy and applied to a real industrial process.

a two-layer linear MPC approach, with a decoupled input selection mechanism, has been developed and successfully applied to a billets heating plant, leading to significant energy and economic savings, and to a more stable operation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed two-layer architecture can effectively be applied in industrial processes where the steady state behavior is strongly coupled to the dynamic behavior.

, when a model is available for the process, it can be used to design and tune a multivariable control strategy that can be easily implemented on the process, leading to significant improvements in the process performance and in the process efficiency.

a decoupled MPC architecture can be successfully applied to industrial processes, providing an easy to use and robust control solution, able to optimize both the steady state and the dynamic behavior of the process, and to reduce the operator intervention.
